previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, asthma, and prior CABG was admitted for a three-week productive cough and one day of sharp, pleuritic chest pain. She presented with uncontrolled hyperglycemia, with blood glucose levels reaching 512 mg/dL. Evaluation revealed no evidence of pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, or acute cardiac ischemia. Chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, exacerbated by coughing. The cough improved with supportive care and was attributed to a viral upper respiratory infection. Her insulin regimen was adjusted with Lantus switched from morning to bedtime dosing, and she received education on proper insulin use. Blood glucose levels stabilized, symptoms resolved, and she was discharged home with services and follow-up arranged for diabetes and blood pressure management.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure taking care of you during your admission to 
___ for chest pain.  You had an urgent cardiac cath which 
showed no new lesions in your coronary arteries. You were 
treated with blood thinners called heparin for a day and your 
symptoms improved and the blood thinner was stopped. Also while 
you were here your kidney function was abnormal compared to what 
it was back in ___. It is likely you have what is called acute 
tubular necrosis and you will need to follow up with your 
primary care doctor about this and monitor your kidney function.

Also you will need to follow up with your dermatologist about 
your skin findings and they drained the cyst on your back. We 
started you on antibiotics to treat the infection which you 
should take for 14 days. The antibiotic is called doxycycline 
and while on it you should avoid the sun.  You have a follow up 
with the dermatologist on ___.

While here your blood sugar levels were a bit elevated so your 
long acting insulin was increased from 50 to 65 units/day. 
It will be important that you get blood work when you see your 
primary care doctor to monitor your kidney function.

While here your blood pressure was elevated most likely because 
your lisinopril was stopped because your kidneys werent working 
as well so we increased your dose of carvedilol to 12.5 mg BID.

We gave you your afternoon meds while here so you will next take 
your meds tomorrow.
